items.title: R. Sridhar, founder of Maithri Trust, passes away at 80
points: Sridhar, founder, Maithri Educational and Charitable Trust, T.
Nagar, passed away on Friday morning after a brief illness.
The last rites were held on Friday evening.
He was afflicted by polio when he was 18 months old, and it left his left hand and both legs paralysed.
The BBC and Deutsche Welle [Voice of Germany] and other channels helped him understand and speak English; and he learnt some Spanish, German, and Hindi.
Though wheelchair-bound, Mr. Sridhar participated in several Citizens’ Runs and used to complete the entire 10 km.
He started Maithri as a trust in 1983 with the lofty dream and an empty pocket.
Mr. Sridhar learned astrology, and when people paid for his services, he would ask them to donate the fee to Maithri Charities, which celebrated its 35th anniversary very recently.

items.title: Plea by suspended Sanskrit varsity students may be amended
points: The Kerala High Court orally enquired whether the petition filed by 16 students of the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit, Kalady, might be amended to include a challenge to the university Syndicate's resolution to revoke suspension on receipt of…
Kunhikrishnan was considering a plea by the suspended students challenging their suspension order and seeking permission to appear for semester examinations.
The Syndicate had also decided to extend the suspension of the remaining four students for two more months.
The matter would be considered again on November 16.
The court sought the response from the petitioners after the university had informed the court of the Syndicate’s decision.
The court had earlier orally enquired why the university’s anger had not subsided even after the students had been suspended for more than 60 days.

The students, Student Federation of India activists, were under suspension pending inquiry for allegedly staging a mock cremation of the Vice-Chancellor, Ciza Thomas, manhandling her and attempting to damage her property.

items.title: Thalassemia-affected children thank Minister Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy for pension initiative
points: A group of children affected by thalassemia met Revenue and Housing Minister Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy and thanked him for his efforts in ensuring the sanction of pensions to them under the Cheyutha Scheme.
The children from various parts of Khammam called on the Minister along with representatives of Sankalpa, a Khammam-based NGO, according to a press release.

The NGO representatives lauded Mr. Reddy for raising the concerns of thalassemia-affected people in Parliament during his tenure as Khammam MP and taking a keen interest in their welfare as a Minister in the State cabinet.

Meanwhile, the Minister distributed new pension sanction orders under the Cheyutha scheme to 1,138 eligible beneficiaries, including widows, elderly persons, weavers and toddy tappers, at a meeting held in Nelakondapalli earlier in the day.

points: Bangladesh and India flags. | Photo Credit: Getty Images/iStockphoto The fifth round of the India-Bangladesh consular dialogue will be held on a “mutually convenient date”, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said on Friday (November 13).

Speaking to the media during the bi-weekly media briefing, Randhir Jaiswal, Official Spokesperson of the MEA, reiterated that India seeks to build “positive, constructive and forward-looking” relations with Bangladesh.
“The next round of the India-Bangladesh Consular Dialogue, which will also take up matters relating to the Revised Travel Arrangement, will be held on a mutually convenient date.
The Hindu had reported on Thursday (November 12) about the postponement of the consular talks that were to be held on November 17 and 18.
Ms. Hasina has been in India since August 5, 2024 and she has said that she would return to Dhaka in December.
The two sides started consular dialogue in 2017 to strengthen people-to-people contact by having a regular channel of communication on consular, visa, and mutual legal assistance cooperation matters.

items.title: Gunmen kill four Naga civilians in Manipur
points: Unidentified gunmen killed four Naga civilians, including a mother and her son, on National Highway 202 in Manipur’s Ukhrul district on Friday (November 13, 2026).
The assailants ambushed the vehicles — a hatchback and a pickup — in New Haven at around 1 p.m.
The location is in the Litan area, the epicentre of conflict between the Kuki and Naga communities since February 2026.
The deceased were identified as Kapangkhui R.S., her son Haoleila R.S., Khanmila Keising, and August Ngalung.

“Additional security forces, comprising Manipur Police, BSF (Border Security Force), Army, and Assam Rifles, have been rushed to the area to reinforce security and prevent any further untoward incidents.
Officials said the site of the attack is about 35 km from Ukhrul town and 6 km short of Litan.
Naga organisations said Kuki armed groups could be behind the attack.
More than 65 people have died since an alleged drunken brawl in February triggered the Kuki-Naga conflict in Manipur.

items.title: Ploughing through the red tape: Inside Ambati Rayudu’s mission to fix Hyderabad cricket
points: Rayudu, the Director of Cricket Operations at the Hyderabad Cricket Association (HCA), shares that satisfaction but remains wary of premature celebrations.
Photo: Special Arrangement Hyderabad cricket has heard many speeches, but few came with a tractor.

In the six months since Ambati Rayudu promised to change the culture, the former India batter has been spotted pitch-side at dawn, at a soil vendor’s door in the rain and, by his own count, five to seven kilos lighter.
The first phase of this Ranji Trophy season has concluded with Hyderabad winning three matches and playing out one draw, enough to put them on top of the Elite Group B table with 20 points.
Rayudu, the Director of Cricket Operations at the Hyderabad Cricket Association (HCA), shares that satisfaction but remains wary of premature celebrations.
It is a long way from May 5, when he walked into a hall of cameras and vowed to take Hyderabad cricket to the next level.

items.title: Navy chief urges Agniveers to aim for full-term service
points: Navy chief Admiral Krishna Swaminathan on Friday urged the service’s latest batch of Agniveers to aspire to a full career in the Indian Navy under the revamped Agnipath scheme unveiled last week, addressing newly inducted sailors at the INS Chilka training…

You now have an additional opportunity to become a regular sailor and build a long and rewarding career in the Indian Navy,” said Swaminathan, who was the chief guest and reviewing officer at a passing-out parade for more than 3,300 recruits, including…

This is the first batch of Agniveers to join the services under the revised Agnipath framework, which offers those not retained an extension of two years in service and another opportunity to qualify for regular service.
Of the lakhs of young aspirants who applied, only about 1.5% made it through, he said.
The new Agnipath framework was cleared by the Cabinet and unveiled by Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani on November 4.

items.title: Koti Deepotsavam begins today, continues till November 30
points: The annual Koti Deepotsavam of Bhakti TV will be held at NTR Stadium near Indira Park from November 14 to 30, coinciding with the auspicious Kartika Masam.

The 17-day spiritual event will be held every day from 5.30 p.m. to 10 p.m., bringing together prominent Jagadgurus, heads of various religious institutions and renowned spiritual speakers, including Chaganti Koteswara Rao and Garikapati Narasimha Rao.
Devotees will have the opportunity to participate in special rituals and perform pujas themselves.
The festival will also feature celestial wedding ceremonies of festival deities from several prominent temples.

Among the major attractions will be Maha Shankhabhishekam, Bhasmabhishekam of Ujjain Mahakaleshwar, special worship of the Somnath Jyotirlinga and darshan of the deities of Kolhapur Mahalakshmi, Kanchi Kamakshi and Madurai Meenakshi temples.
The organisers said all essential materials required for the rituals, including wicks, oil and earthen lamps, would also be provided to devotees free of cost.

items.title: Vigilance detects irregularities at Kasaragod port office
points: Four alleged irregularities, including unauthorised appointments, diversion of sand permits, use of boats with expired licences for sand mining, and discrepancies in financial records, were detected during a Vigilance inspection at the Kasaragod Port Office.
The Vigilance team found that employees had been appointed on a daily wage basis without government orders or approval from the competent authorities since 2017.
Such employees had been deployed for work at river ghats as well as the port office.
The team examined documents relating to these appointments.
The inspection also revealed that sand had been allotted to individuals using building permits without the knowledge or consent of the actual owners.
The team found that the validity of the licences of boats currently being used for sand mining had expired on August 31, 2026.
The Vigilance authorities are scrutinising the findings and documents collected to initiate further action.

items.title: Mahatma Gandhi University in Keralam imposes restrictions on media access
points: Updated - November 13, 2026 10:29 pm IST - THIRUVANANTHAPURAM The Mahatma Gandhi University has introduced strict restrictions on media access.
A circular issued by the University Registrar states that those seeking to enter the university campus for news coverage must secure the Vice-Chancellor’s approval in advance.
The Kerala Union of Working Journalists (KUWJ) has condemned the ‘anti-democratic” restrictions imposed on the media at the university.
The union stated that the Vice-Chancellor’s order was effectively an attempt to muzzle the press.
It added that such arbitrary orders should not be issued by a university, which is expected to be a centre of democratic values and independent thought.
The union also pointed out that media restrictions of this nature are extremely rare.
The KUWJ also stated that a university named after Mahatma Gandhi imposing restrictions on civil rights sends a deeply condemnable message.

items.title: Markapuram, Prakasam, Nellore districts get ready for Panchayat elections
points: As the Andhra Pradesh State Election Commission has issued an official notification for the conduct of elections in 23 Urban Local Bodies across the State, Markapuram, Prakasam, and Nellore district administrations prepare for the Gram Panchayat elections.
In Markapuram district, elections will be held for Podili Nagar Panchayat.
Nominations will be accepted from November 14 to 16, and the scrutiny of nominations will take place on November 17.
Raja Babu said that Gram Panchayat elections will be conducted for 519 panchayats across three divisions and 27 mandals in the district; following the merger of Dasarivaripalem.
There are 10.70 lakh voters in the district, he stated.

The polling will take place across 139 panchayats in Ongole and Kondapi constituencies during the first phase, across 198 panchayats in Addanki and Darsi constituencies in second phase, and 178 panchayats in Kandukuru and S.N.

items.title: Court rejects police plea to cancel bail of CPI(M) workers in ED officials’ attack case
points: The petition sought the cancellation of the bail granted to Nithin Raj, the first accused, and former Thiruvananthapuram Corporation councillor I.P.
The prosecution argued that the accused persons violated their bail conditions by allegedly participating in the Onam celebrations held at the Museum police station.
The controversy arose when the two accused visited the police station to comply with the bail condition that requires them to appear and sign their attendance as directed by the court.
During the visit, they reportedly took part in the Onam celebrations.
It observed that the accused had visited the police station to fulfil the requirement of signing as part of their bail conditions.

Their brief participation in the Onam festivities, including riding the swing and playing the chenda, could be considered part of the celebrations and did not, by itself, constitute a violation of the bail conditions.
Both accused also strongly opposed the prosecution’s plea, and the court dismissed the application after considering their arguments.

items.title: Faridabad: Cop's son fires gunshots in road rage; two injured
points: A policeman's son allegedly opened fire at two brothers in a road rage near the Central Bank on Kacha Kheri Road here, authorities said on Friday.
One received a gunshot wound in the neck, and the other in his chest.
Both are under treatment at a hospital in Sector-21 A.
The police have arrested 28-year-old Jaswant, the alleged shooter, a resident of Bharat Colony, Faridabad.
According to the police, on Thursday, around 9.20 pm, Piyush, a resident of the same colony as Jaswant, was on his way to a railway station in Delhi.
His cousins Prashant, Prince, and Tushar were with him in the car.
While on the way, Piyush honked at an oncoming Maruti Brezza car to give way, but the driver, allegedly Jaswant, blocked the road by positioning his vehicle in front of Piyush's car.
"Preliminary interrogation revealed that following a dispute over giving way to a vehicle, the accused fired four rounds from his licensed revolver, hitting Prashant and Prince.

items.title: Graduation Day celebrated at St. Joseph’s College of Education in Mysuru
points: St. Joseph’s College of Education, Jayalakshmipuram, celebrated the Graduation Day of its 54th batch on the college premises here on Friday.

Graduation oath was administered by Edward William Saldanha, secretary and correspondent, MDES, who, later in his address, emphasised on the ethical responsibilities, professional commitment, and dedication expected from future educators.
Noting that while a good teacher teaches lessons, a great teacher transforms lives, he urged them not to discriminate and compare them unfairly.
Discover the goodness in each one of them and help them bring out the best within themselves, he advised.

Prathima, regional joint director, Department of Collegiate Education, Mysuru, highlighted the role of modern tech tools and observed that while AI can tell a student what to learn, a great teacher helps them understand why learning matters.
She emphasised that a harmonious combination of technology, dedicated teachers, and human values can transform the future of education.
All graduating teacher trainees were presented with their Graduation Scrolls by the dignitaries.

items.title: One killed, four injured as lorry rams into MLC Teenmar Mallanna’s convoy in Yadadri-Bhongir district
points: One woman was killed and four others were injured after a speeding lorry rammed into a vehicle in the convoy of Telangana Rajyadhikara Party MLC Teenmar Mallanna in Yadadri-Bhongir district on Friday.
The accident occurred at around 10.45 a.m. at Anajipuram village in Mothkur mandal when the convoy was proceeding towards Tirumalagiri via the village.
The lorry hit a Toyota Fortuner, that was part of the convoy, from the rear.
Mallanna escaped unhurt as his vehicle was away from the spot of impact.
The Fortuner rammed into a hatchback, injuring 24-year-old Chandana, and her husband Medaboyina Srinath.
Two others, identified as Bunny and Ranganna, who were travelling in the MLC’s car, were also injured.
A case was registered under Section 125(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).

points: Union Minister of Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari addressing a session at the 31st CII Partnership Summit in Visakhapatnam on Friday. | Photo Credit: V.

RAJU Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari on Friday asserted that world-class road infrastructure is the foundation for India’s economic progress, and particularly for the holistic development of Andhra Pradesh.

Mr. Gadkari delivered the keynote address at a session on the theme ‘Roads to Viksit Bharat: Highways, Logistics, Andhra Pradesh Growth Corridor” on the second day of the 31st CII Partnership Summit here.

On the road development projects in Andhra Pradesh, Mr. Gadkari said the ​1,100 km Surat–Chennai Expressway, being built at a cost of ₹45,000 crore, will pass through Kadapa, Annamayya, and Tirupati districts.

items.title: Kakinada Mayor race heats up, all eyes on JSP’s candidate choice
points: Harendhira Prasad Kakinada District Collector | Photo Credit: GIRI KVS All eyes are on the Mayor candidate of the NDA alliance in the Kakinada Municipal Corporation as the Jana Sena Party (JSP) is yet to announce its candidate.
The JPS secured the Kakinada Mayor seat during the seat-sharing arrangement among the NDA alliance partners.
However, the Mayor's post has been reserved for a woman from the Backward Classes, including fisherfolk community, who have a significant presence in the Jana Sena party.
Nomination for the Mayor’s post will be accepted from November 14 to 16, and candidates can withdraw their nominations by November 19.
Meanwhile, YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) has fielded Kakinada-based doctor Kada Satya Sri as their candidate.
She joined the party in the presence of YSRCP president Y.S.Jagan Mohan Reddy on November 12.
Sunkara Siva Prasanna of the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) served as the last Mayor of Kakinada Municipal Corporation in 2021.
In 2017, Sunkara Pavani of TDP was elected Mayor.

items.title: Eight Army personnel injured as military truck overturns near Chevella
points: Eight Indian Army personnel sustained serious injuries after a military truck carrying 14 soldiers overturned near Allawada village in Chevella on Friday morning.
The accident occurred at around 9.40 a.m. when the personnel were travelling from the Golconda Army camp towards Shabad as part of a training exercise.
A trainee soldier was reportedly driving the vehicle when it went out of control, hit a road divider and overturned.
The truck reportedly rolled over several times before crashing into a tree and coming to a halt.
Eight personnel suffered serious injuries and were shifted to a hospital in Golconda for treatment.
No police complaint has been registered in connection with the incident.

points: The Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) has criticised the unilateral decision of Chief Minister A.
Revanth Reddy to scrap the Intermediate education system from the next academic year and introduce the new system of 10+2 without any Cabinet decision, Bill in legislature and discussion on it.

He alleged that the main beneficiaries of the decision would be corporate educational institutions’ groups such as Narayana and Sri Chaitanya.
The private colleges which offer only Intermediate courses would face closure and the decision was entirely business-oriented and helpful to corporate groups including the Chief Minister A.

items.title: Demolition of nearly century-old colonial-era building at BCU decried
points: The university has stated that the building, which was over 90 years old, was in a severely dilapidated condition and was demolished based on an expert report. | Photo Credit: K.

MURALI KUMAR Dr. Manmohan Singh Bengaluru City University (DMSBCU) has demolished a two-storey building with Victorian architecture that housed the Indian Council of Historical Research (ICHR) office and was only a few years short of completing a century.
The university stated that the building, which was over 90 years old, was in a severely dilapidated condition and was demolished based on an expert report.
The building in question was modelled on the University Union Building at Mysore University, built in 1920.
Ten years later, in 1930, an almost identical building, the University Union of Central College, was inaugurated in Bengaluru.
Located at the intersection of Palace Road and Kempe Gowda Road, the building had a reading room and library as well as facilities for table tennis, draughts and chess.

items.title: Oil India on track for 4 MMT crude oil production this fiscal, officials state
points: Oil India is confident of achieving its crude oil production target of 4 million metric tonnes (MMT) in the current fiscal, with output expected to rise further in the succeeding years, company officials said during an analyst call on Friday.
“The point is that we are on a path to four and are very confident that we will achieve [the same] this year.
Our internal targets are a little bit more, but we are targeting four and are on that path,” officials said.
The state-owned oil and gas explorer is also expecting a modest increase in natural gas production this fiscal.
However, a more significant boost is anticipated following the commissioning of the Duliajan feeder line in about 18-20 months.
Meanwhile, Numaligarh Refinery, a material subsidiary of Oil India, is targeting capital expenditure of ₹6,000 crore in the next fiscal as it moves towards completing its ongoing projects.

items.title: J&K Police zero in on LeT operative, two foreigners in Kulgam CRPF attack
points: Security personnel arrive as a cordon and search operation continues for the second day following a terror attack on a CRPF checkpoint near Mir Bazar, in Kulgam district, Jammu and Kashmir, November 12, 2026.
Senior police officials said they have “credible leads” pointing to the involvement of Bhat, a carpenter from Kulgam.
He is also wanted for two attacks in Anantnag and Kulgam last July that left a police officer and two workers from Chhattisgarh dead.
Officials said they are examining Bhat’s digital footprint, and multiple leads point to two foreigners being involved in the attack.
They also used AK-47 rifles and fired from close range.
The security agencies said Bhat made a daring escape after the Anantnag attack in July this year.
A National Investigation Agency (NIA) team visited the Kulgam site on Friday (November 13, 2026) to gather evidence and establish the attackers’ mode of operation.

items.title: Two Tamil Nadu traders arrested over alleged diversion of 11,000 litres of Sabarimala ghee
points: The ghee, supplied by the Kerala Co-operative Milk Marketing Federation (KCMMF), which markets its products under the brand name Milma, was allegedly diverted by a contractor and sold to the traders for around ₹50 lakh.

The two traders, Venkateswaran and Kumaran, have been accused of buying ghee allegedly diverted by a contractor from official Milma consignments meant for the Sabarimala temple during the 2025 pilgrimage season.
KCMMF had bagged the tender to supply ghee to the hill shrine located in Pathanamthitta district.

An official said that SS Binu, the contractor who was arrested last month, had diverted around 11,000 litres of ghee from the official KCMMF consignment meant for the temple and sold the stock to the two Tamil Nadu traders for around ₹50 lakh.
After diverting the stock of ghee, Binu had allegedly supplied a cheaper form of ghee to the temple, causing a loss of ₹2.5 crore to the Travancore Devaswom Board (TDB), which administers the temple.

items.title: Telangana Women’s Commission issues notices to eight ART centres in illegal oocyte racket case
points: The Commission examined representatives of the eight institutions on Friday, November 13, after directing their managements to appear before it.

However, TGSCW Chairperson Nerella Sharada expressed dissatisfaction after some centres sent staff members and other representatives instead of senior management, despite being specifically instructed to attend in person.
The inquiry was subsequently adjourned after the institutions assured the Commission that their management would appear at the next hearing.
During Friday’s proceedings, the Commission scrutinised reports, records and details of egg donors submitted by the ART centres and egg banks.

She also questioned claims made by the institutions that nearly 90% of their egg donors came from other States and donated their eggs voluntarily without receiving any remuneration or financial compensation.

Commissioner of Health and Family Welfare, Sangeetha Satyanarayana, also attended the inquiry, during which Ms. Sharada sought details about the progress of the department’s investigation into the alleged illegal egg procurement practices.

items.title: KIIFB accounts should have been audited by CAG, says Kerala High Court
points: The previous State government’s decision not to entrust the audit of the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board (KIIFB) to the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) is more than concerning, observed the Kerala High Court.
The Division Bench of Chief Justice Soumen Sen and Justice V.M.
Syam Kumar stated that the previous government should have allowed the audit, especially with regard to the “enormous discrepancies” noticed in the preliminary report.
The court held that transparency must be maintained in the accounts and functioning of the KIIFB since it was funded by the State, which furnished guarantees for its borrowings.
The court also expressed displeasure at KIIFB’s adverse stance against the CAG audit.
The court noted that the present government had resolved to restructure KIIFB and as per the recommendations of an expert committee, have the CAG audit the KIIFB accounts comprehensively.

items.title: Farmers demand water supply for crops till Dec. 30
points: Hundreds of farmers took out a procession from Gandhi Bhavan to the Deputy Commissioner’s office where they staged a demonstration against the proposed discontinuation of canal water supply on November 20.
Addressing the protesters, AIKKMS district president Govinda said that farmers have invested heavily in cultivation by borrowing money amid rising input costs.
With crops nearing maturity, stopping water supply on November 20 will deprive them of the opportunity to harvest their produce, he said.
He pointed out that more than 96 tmcft of water has been stored in the Tungabhadra reservoir this year and questioned the State government’s decision not to ensure water supply even for one crop.
AIKKMS district secretary Guralli Raj said that water is being illegally supplied through motors to several industries, while the State government is unwilling to ensure adequate water for crops.
Warning of a more intense protest after November 20, he said that the State government will be held responsible for the consequences of stopping water supply for crops.

items.title: TVK Karamadai union secretary booked on sexual harassment charge
points: The police have registered a case against Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam’s (TVK) Karamadai union secretary for alleged sexual harassment of a woman functionary, and against a couple in the party for subjecting her to caste-based harassment.
A panchayat level secretary of the party, aged 29, raised the allegation against Karamadai union secretary Karupusamy.

items.title: BCAS wants CA firms to monitor use of IPO proceeds
points: The Bombay Chartered Accountants’ Society has submitted recommendations to SEBI on monitoring agencies, public issue proceeds and disclosure requirements.
In its representation on SEBI’s proposals, BCAS said the requirement would significantly increase the workload for monitoring agencies.
Currently, only credit rating agencies registered with SEBI can undertake this role.

Allowing CA firms holding a valid peer review certificate from the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) to act as monitoring agencies, at least for issues below a specified size, would help expand capacity, it said.
Such firms are subject to auditing standards, quality control requirements and ICAI’s disciplinary jurisdiction, and have experience in verifying the application of funds.

It also proposes aligning the monitoring and disclosure requirements under the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations and the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations.

items.title: Cyclone 'Senyar' Brewing In Bay of Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Andhra On Alert
points: A new cyclonic storm, likely to be named 'Senyar', is brewing in the Bay of Bengal.
Under the influence of an upper-air cyclonic circulation, a low-pressure area formed over the Southeast Bay of Bengal on Friday, signaling the start of a rapidly evolving weather system.
The system is likely to move northwestwards and intensify into a well-marked low-pressure area by Saturday, followed by a depression over the same region by Sunday morning.
It is then likely to move north-northwestwards and may intensify into a cyclonic storm over the central Bay of Bengal by Monday evening.
This comes two weeks after cyclone 'Arnab' hit India and made landfall as a "very severe" cyclonic storm, the third-highest category on IMD's scale.
Five people were killed in separate incidents linked to the cyclone in Andhra Pradesh in Vizag, Anakapalle, Kakinada, Konaseema and West Godavari.

points: The Leading Maritime Cities (LMC) 2026 report, compiled by DNV and Menon Economics, benchmarks the world’s leading maritime cities to identify where maritime companies and professionals have the strongest environment to connect, operate and grow.

Together, these provide a broad view of the capabilities and conditions that shape a city’s position in the global maritime industry.

Now in its seventh edition, the report has evolved from benchmarking where maritime activity is concentrated to assessing which cities are best positioned to combine maritime scale with the capacity to adapt to changing industry conditions.

items.title: Diwali gains often last. Will this year’s Sensex rally hold?
points: The BSE Sensex gained 0.73% in the week after Muhurat trading on 8 November, adding to its strongest pre-Diwali weekly rally in three decades.

In 2010, the Sensex gained 4.86% before Muhurat but lost 4.04% afterwards.
A year earlier, a 4.11% rise was followed by a 2.96% decline.
In 2001, the Sensex rose 3.29% before Muhurat and another 5.42% afterwards.

items.title: LAYUPMAN revision reaches key milestone in London

items.title: IACS Publishes New Recommendation on Gas Dispersion Analysis (Rec.202)
points: IACS, the membership organisation for the world’s leading classification societies, has published a new Recommendation on gas dispersion analysis, marking a further significant contribution in its support of the safe decarbonisation of the maritime industry.
The new guidance provides information on the best practices and requirements for carrying out gas dispersion analysis for Ships using gaseous fuels such as Ammonia and Hydrogen.

Rec.202 is another significant deliverable from the IACS Safe Decarbonisation Panel and draws on several years of technical work and engagement with fuel manufacturers, technology providers, shipowners, shipbuilders, marine insurers and flag States.

It provides a critical technical framework to support the safe use of alternative fuels such as ammonia and hydrogen, helping the maritime industry transition responsibly toward cleaner energy solutions.

Rec.202 constitutes the first output arising from such a joint undertaking.

items.title: IMTRA Announces Leadership And Organizational Changes To Support Continued Growth
points: IMTRA, the leading manufacturer and importer of quality solutions and products for the marine, energy and transportation markets, announced today that Vice President of Recreational Sales Chip Farnham will retire after more than 40 years with the company.

Alongside his retirement, IMTRA announced leadership and organizational changes designed to strengthen coordination across its sales, product management and operational functions and support continued growth.
Farnham’s grandfather founded IMTRA, and his family held an ownership stake for 70 years.
Throughout his career, Farnham has played an important role in IMTRA’s growth, building lasting relationships with customers and partners throughout the marine industry.

items.title: CYTUR and PLAINBIT Sign MOU to Strengthen Maritime Cyber Incident Investigation and Response
points: CYTUR Inc. (CEO Yonghyun Jo), a maritime cybersecurity specialist, announced that it signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with Plainbit Co. , Ltd. (CEO Jinkook Kim), a company specializing in digital forensics and incident response, on November 11, 2026.

items.title: Turkey – Environmental Pollution Fines: Updated for 2027
points: Environmental pollution fines in Turkish waters will increase by 27.83% from 1 January 2027.

The revised fines apply to pollution offences under Turkish Environmental Code No. 2872, including discharges of petroleum products, oily waste, dirty ballast, sewage, washwater, garbage and cargo residues.
Fine amounts are calculated according to the vessel’s gross tonnage and the nature of the pollutant.
Increased penalties may apply to repeat offences, pollution involving hazardous substances and incidents within designated Special Environmental Protection Areas.
Members trading to or through Turkish waters should review their pollution-prevention procedures and ensure that crews take appropriate measures to prevent accidental discharges.
Particular care should be taken during deballasting, deck washing and shipyard or dry-dock operations.

items.title: IAPH2026: tools launched to support decarbonisation
points: During the 2026 World Ports Conference in London last week, IAPH released a suite of tools to add vital momentum to the port industry’s ambitions to decarbonise.
Developed by the working groups of the IAPH Climate and Energy committee, the tools were unveiled during special sessions at the conference.
The first tool is an upgrade of an existing IAPH product for ports: Port Readiness Level assessment tool for Bunkering Clean Marine Fuels (PRL Bunkering).
An upgrade on the version released in 2023, it has benefited from use and feedback by IAPH member ports.
It can be accessed at fuelreadyports.org The second is the Port Readiness Level assessment tool for Clean Fuel Cargo (PRL Cargo).
It has been put together by IAPH’s PRL Working Group to complement the CEM-HUBs report by ICS and IAPH, ahead of the upcoming full Ministerial Call for action report in the New Year.

items.title: Long Beach: Emissions Driven to Lowest Levels in Port’s Busiest Year
points: Strategic investments in zero-emissions equipment, greater use of shore power and more frequent visits by cleaner ships have driven the Port of Long Beach’s emissions per container to an all-time low, even as the global trade hub moved record-breaking…

items.title: MPA Opens Applications for LNG Floating Storage Unit Licences in Singapore
points: The Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) has opened applications for licences to operate up to two liquefied natural gas (LNG) Floating Storage Units (FSUs) in Singapore anchorages.
The call for applications follows MPA’s award of eight new LNG bunker supplier licences in July 2026[1].

To support the continued growth of LNG bunkering services in Singapore and strengthen supply resilience, the FSUs will complement the expanded supplier base by diversifying LNG storage and reloading options.
Key FSU Licensing Requirements Applications are open to existing LNG bunker licensees, who may partner third-party terminal operators to provide the necessary storage and operational expertise.

Most of the FSU’s storage capacity must be allocated for LNG bunkering and there will be a minimum requirement for capacity that must be made available to other LNG bunker suppliers on open-access terms.

Applicants must own or charter at least one FSU with a minimum storage capacity of 130,000 m³, registered with the Singapore Registry of Ships, and comply with MPA’s safety and operational requirements.

items.title: Chinese-backed Simandou iron ore project in Guinea makes major progress
points: China Baowu Steel Group (CBSG) announced on Thursday that the north section of the Simandou iron ore and infrastructure project in Guinea, a world-class hematite deposit, has been completed and entered operation.
The mine project, operated by the Chinese-backed Baowu Winning Consortium Simandou, has completed the full-line heavy-load trial run of its second series downhill conveyor system.
The Simandou project officially commenced operations in Guinea in November 2025.
With a total cost of approximately $20 billion, the project brings together industry giants, including Rio Tinto, Chinalco, and CBSG, and spans mining operations, railways and ports.
Located in southeastern Guinea in west Africa, the Simandou deposit stretches about 110 kilometers along a mountain range.

items.title: Former Madras HC judge CS Karnan, first sitting judge jailed for contempt, dies at 71
points: Former Madras High Court judge CS Karnan, the first sitting high court judge to be sentenced to imprisonment for contempt of court, died on Friday morning at a private hospital here following age-related health complications.
Karnan practised as a lawyer before being appointed additional judge of the Madras High Court in March 2009, and was elevated to permanent judge in March 2011.
As friction with his colleagues mounted, the Supreme Court collegium recommended his transfer to the Calcutta High Court in February 2016.

The confrontation with the Supreme Court escalated in January 2017, when justice Karnan wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, accusing 20 sitting and retired judges of corruption and seeking action against them.

A seven-judge bench of the Supreme Court headed by then Chief Justice of India JS Khehar initiated suo motu contempt proceedings in February 2017 and stripped him of all judicial and administrative powers.
In May 2018, he announced the launch of a political party, ‘Anti-Corruption Dynamic Party’.

points: A woman from Mumbai’s Bhandup area was allegedly defrauded of ₹90.79 lakhs by imposters for nearly three years between 2023 and 2025 on pretext of a ‘data entry’ job, following which the East Region Cyber Police filed an extortion case against unknown…
It began in 2023 when the woman was looking for a job and came across a data entry job opportunity online.

Trusting their claims, the woman filled the form and three days after making the first payment, she received a WhatsApp call from a woman to discuss the data entry job.
Driven by fear, the victim began making payments, a process that continued from 2023 through December 2024.

items.title: Manipur 2023 violence probe panel gets another extension; asked to submit report by May 20
points: New Delhi, The Centre has given another six-month extension, till May 20 next year, to a Commission of Inquiry to submit its report on the probe into the 2023 Manipur violence that claimed more than 260 lives, a government notification said.

The three-member panel, now headed by former Supreme Court judge Balbir Singh Chauhan, was formed on June 4, 2023, in the aftermath of the ethnic violence that broke out in the northeastern state in May that year.

items.title: Mahindra Sets New SUV Sales Record: 73,338 Units Sold In October

items.title: Gujarat BJP MLA's Nephew Arrested 40 Hours After Range Rover Killed Biker
points: The nephew of a BJP MLA in Gujarat has been arrested for allegedly killing one person and injuring another in a road accident while driving his Range Rover.

items.title: Low-pressure area in Bay of Bengal likely to intensify into cyclonic storm by November 16: IMD
points: A low-pressure area, formed over the southeast Bay of Bengal, is likely to intensify gradually and become a cyclonic storm by November 16 (Monday) evening, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said on Friday.
The system formed at 5.30 am under the influence of an upper-air cyclonic circulation over the central Andaman Sea and adjoining Andaman and Nicobar Islands, according to the weather agency.
"The low-pressure area over the southeast Bay of Bengal is likely to move northwestwards and intensify into a depression by November 15," it said.
The system is expected to move northwestwards and develop into a well-marked low-pressure area around November 14.
Wind speeds of around 50 kmph and gusts reaching 60 kmph are likely over the Andaman Sea on November 13 and 14, and over the southeast Bay of Bengal between November 13 and 16.

points: BW LPG has struck another lucrative vessel sale, offloading a VLGC acquired in John Fredriksen’s Avance Gas fleet deal less than two years ago for well over $100m.

items.title: UK blacklists 11 ships in fresh Russia sanctions sweep
points: Britain has slapped fresh sanctions on 11 ships linked to Russian energy exports, targeting five LNG carriers, five oil tankers and a floating storage unit in its latest effort to disrupt Moscow’s seaborne oil and gas trade.
The measures also cover nine companies, including Russian oil producer Slavneft, Rosneft’s Vostok Oil project and several energy trading businesses based in Dubai.

items.title: Deutsche Windtechnik picked for UK offshore wind maintenance job
points: German offshore wind services specialist Deutsche Windtechnik has secured a five-year operations and maintenance contract covering two offshore wind farms in the UK.
The agreement, awarded by asset manager XceCo, covers the Lynn and Inner Dowsing wind farms off Lincolnshire, which have a combined installed capacity of 194.4MW.

points: Maharashtra authorities have taken action by seizing beauty creams in Nanded that contained alarmingly high levels of mercury, valued at Rs 40 lakh.

Officials have issued a public alert against usage, and a legal case under drug safety regulations has been filed.
